title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency investment scam. The scheme began with unsolicited contact through WhatsApp and used a real mobile trading app overlaid with an AI-generated fake website that displayed false account balances and transaction history. The scammers built trust by allowing small initial withdrawals before stealing the bulk of the funds.

This is a case of impersonation and deception at the point where a user sees information on screen. The system that failed was not the trading app itself, which police confirmed was real, but the visual layer presented to the user. What would have caught this: verification of withdrawal requests through a separate channel, or a security check that confirmed account balances through the app's actual backend before processing transactions rather than relying on what appeared on the user's screen.

It is not established whether the app developers were aware their platform was being used this way, or whether any AI system was involved beyond the creation of the fake website displayed to the victim.

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. Jerry Dunaway was convinced to invest using a mobile trading app, and the scammers built his trust by allowing him to see small profits and withdraw funds initially. The scheme used an AI-generated fake website that displayed false investment balances on his screen while the scammers stole his money.

The couple discovered the fraud when Jerry tried to withdraw additional funds and couldn't access the money. Gwinnett County police confirmed the app was real, but scammers had created a deceptive overlay showing fake account information. The Dunaways are now warning others about these sophisticated tactics and working with police, though investigators say victims rarely recover stolen funds in such cases. Their children created a GoFundMe page to help the couple with daily expenses.
